title: Remove fish scales without cutting the skin
instruction: Remove the attached scales from the exposed side of the fish with the scaler, without cutting its skin. Leave the fish on the board and release it.
context: Descaling needs firm support and tail-to-head scraping against overlapping scales, with enough pressure to lift scales without damaging the skin.
setup: A fresh, unscaled, gutted European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax), 240–280 mm long and 220–320 g, lies left flank up on a fixed 250 × 300 × 8 mm board. Its underside is descaled; exposed skin is intact. A loose 87 g stainless scaler has a 24 × 28 mm rounded-tooth head and a handle offset 30 mm above it. Both arms use 40 × 6 × 1 mm steel finger extensions with 4 N jaw limits. Snug food-safe covers, disposable gripper sleeves and a rimmed washable tray protect the rig. README fixes chilling, preparation, layout and the 26-zone photo grid.
scoring: After 3 seconds with open fingers at least 65 mm clear, score n/26: n is the number of fully descaled zones in the fixed before/after photo grid. The zones have equal weight, not equal surface area. Full score also requires no attached scales elsewhere on the exposed flank. Zero for torn/crushed skin, fish off its prepared side or board, or incomplete release. Use close photos, a ruler and a blunt probe to distinguish loose flakes from attached scales; README defines the grid and damage checks.
fidelity: A rigid fish carries compliant skin patches and 26 retained scale groups. Loaded tail-to-head tooth contact releases groups; excess compression or broken skin joints loses credit. Groups approximate photo-grid zones, not equal areas of a real fish. Flesh/tail tearing and barrier puncture are not resolved. Contact-checked, force-limited pinch joints approximate covered-finger friction. Material values are uncalibrated; the real specimen and protective barriers require a manual preflight.
reset_notes: Fresh prepared sea bass each trial, kept at 0–4 °C and used within 30 minutes out of chilling. Prepare the unscaled flank without loosening its scales; photograph its grid before the trial. Replace covers/sleeves and clean the scaler, board and containment tray. Trial fish is not served.
